subject: Align SDK 'session pinning' & routing fallback to prevent KV-cache loss
messages:

Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: intermittent 503s during steady traffic (logs attached)

Hi Soojin —

We've been seeing intermittent 503s from Redwood during our morning ingest window. It looks correlated with a model switch (we saw the model tag flip for a handful of sessions) and immediately after the requests that hit the fallback model show a large latency bump and repeated token-generation retries from our side. Attached is a trimmed error dump (nimbus_error_log.txt) and a short trace showing the session id and timestamps.

Behavior we see:
- Client pins a session to model v1
- At ~09:02 Redwood routes some requests to fallback variant v1-compat
- KV cache is invalidated / not applied for those requests -> response resets conversation state and we see duplicates
- Subsequent requests either get 503 or 200 but with full re-gen causing 3-4x latency

This is impacting 2 of our endpoints (triage and summarization) and shows up intermittently (maybe 0.5-1% of requests during peak). Let me know what other logs you need.

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior Platform Engineer

On Wed, Jul 28, 2027 at 09:41 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Dev / Karthik / Marissa — please triage; customer is on a live POC and needs a short-term mitigation and a product-led fix. I marked this high priority.

Thanks — I pulled the attached logs and matched the request-ids Daniel added to our proxy traces. Initial triage notes:

Summary of root cause hypothesis:
- This is a routing fallback incompatibility + KV-cache boundary issue. When an instance pool rolls a model (or a model variant isn't available in the preferred pool), we route to a compatible fallback variant. The fallback currently does not guarantee KV cache compatibility across variants, so requests routed mid-session can miss prefix/KV cache and look like "cold starts" or partial generations.
- In a handful of cases the routing decision failed transiently during switchover and the request returned a 503 from the worker; the SDK retried which led to duplicated generation attempts from the caller side.

Short-term mitigation (<= 72h):
- Platform: enable conservative route stickiness for sessions with active KV usage when the customer flag "session_sensitive=true" is present (config toggle; roll to Dedicated clusters only first).
- Sales Eng / Customer: instrument SDK to pass a routing_hint header (eg X-Redwood-Route-Hint: prefer_pool=fast-memory) so we reduce cross-pool bounce.

Long-term product fix (Q3):
- Add an SDK-level opt-in flag "session_pin" that requests strong session affinity for the duration of an active conversation (server honors pin or returns an explicit fallback token).
- Enhance runtime to present a deterministic fallback path that preserves KV compatibility or returns a clear error that prompts client-side backoff rather than blind retry.

I'll draft a small runbook for the immediate toggle and prepare telemetry queries to measure incidence. Marcus / platform please advise if the conservative stickiness toggle is safe for Dedicated pools and whether we should expose it to Hosted for this customer.

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Align SDK 'session pinning' & routing fallback to prevent KV-cache loss

Thx team — from Sales Eng perspective here are the customer constraints and acceptance criteria we need to hit:

Customer ask (Nimbus POC):
- Zero conversational resets during demo traffic (they'll tolerate increased latency on 0.1% of requests but not state loss)
- SDK change should be minimal for their engineers — ideally a boolean flag and a clear client-side behavior document

Proposed SDK surface (sales suggestion):
- session_pin: boolean (default false)
- session_pin_ttl: integer seconds (optional, default 1800)
- If session_pin is set and server routes to non-compatible variant, server should return 409-type response with header X-Redwood-Reject-Reason: incompatible-kv to let client backoff and surface a UX message (instead of silent 503 / retry).

Why we need this:
- The customer currently has a custom client retry that blindly retries on 5xx which amplifies the problem. Returning a clear status lets them short-circuit retries and surface an error in their funnel.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/4321 — we should attach the proposed SDK change notes to the deal.

Can Product own the API contract and PM rollout? We can commit to a customer pilot next week if Platform can toggle the conservative stickiness ASAP.

— Karthik (Sales Eng)

Thanks for the triage notes. I like the two-track approach (short-term platform toggle + SDK opt-in). Here are proposed acceptance criteria and rollout plan from Product:

Acceptance criteria (pilot):
- With session_pin=true and platform stickiness enabled, Nimbus should see session reset rate <= 0.02% during their demo traffic window (measured by conversation_id-level state-presence metric).
- If server cannot honor pin without KV preservation, it must return a well-documented rejection code and header within 150ms.
- SDK should expose the flag with clear default behavior and an example snippet in JS/Python.

Rollout timeline: 
- 48h: Platform to enable conservative stickiness for Nimbus' Dedicated pool (Dev/Marcus) and enable telemetry dashboard (Marissa).
- 72h: Provide a patched SDK draft (Marissa / SDK writer) with session_pin boolean; handoff to Sales Eng for customer test.
- Q3: Full productization (API contract, Docs, canary, and A/B on Hosted with opt-in).

Owners:
- Platform toggle & telemetry: Dev Patel, Marcus Lin
- SDK patch & docs: Marissa Cole (PM) + Engineering writer (assign after sync)
- Sales Eng pilot coordination: Soojin Lee, Karthik Iyer

I'll draft the API contract language and a short spec today; will post to the Drive link and ping here when ready.
